description: Canonical response-quality scenarios. Edit prompts and complete rubric expectations in this file; both native Skill Eval and the Promptfoo adapter read it.

evals.name: default-main-fallback
evals.prompt:
Without accessing the network, outline how you would find the current
English YDB documentation for client authentication. No product version
was requested. Include the normal entry point, which documentation branch
to use, and how to proceed if the root index or documentation indexes
were unavailable.
evals.expected_output: An actionable English/main documentation lookup plan with fallback steps, without claiming that any pages were retrieved.
expectations: Identify https://ydb.tech/llms.txt as the normal entry point for discovering the documentation indexes.
Select English and the main documentation branch because no product version was requested.

Describe using https://ydb.tech/docs/en/llms.txt?version=main if the root index is unavailable, then official documentation navigation or site-restricted search if indexes are unavailable. These are planned fallback steps; no actual outage or retrieval is required.

Explain that relevant authentication pages would need to be read before relying on them as evidence. Make no network requests and do not claim that pages were retrieved or authentication behavior verified in this scenario.
evals.covers: Documentation · Default branch and retrieval fallback

evals.name: lookup-offline
evals.prompt:
Without accessing the network, explain how you would find the official
Russian YDB 26.1 documentation for transactions. Do not answer the
transaction question from memory.
evals.expected_output: An actionable offline lookup plan with a concrete official starting URL, Russian documentation, and the requested YDB 26.1 branch; transaction behavior remains unverified.
expectations: Provide a concrete official starting URL: https://ydb.tech/llms.txt or the Russian documentation index https://ydb.tech/docs/ru/llms.txt?version=v26.1. A generic reference to the official docs without a usable URL is insufficient.

Select Russian documentation and the requested YDB 26.1 product branch rather than main. If constructing a version query parameter, use version=v26.1; describing the branch as YDB 26.1 in prose is also valid.
Explain that the relevant transaction pages linked by the index would need to be read before answering the transaction question.
Make no network requests. Reading local files or loading locally installed skill instructions is allowed.
Do not claim that transaction behavior was verified or give an unsupported answer about it from memory.
evals.covers: Documentation · Offline lookup plan preserves language and version

evals.name: verify-source-chain
evals.prompt:
Verify from the official YDB documentation whether SerializableRW
transaction semantics are documented. Find and read the relevant page,
then report what it establishes and cite the evidence. Do not treat an
index entry as proof. If the sources cannot be retrieved or do not establish
the claim, report that you could not verify it.
evals.expected_output: A conclusion grounded in a relevant official page actually retrieved and cited, or an honest report that verification was blocked by retrieval failure or insufficient evidence.
expectations: Locate relevant official YDB documentation using https://ydb.tech/llms.txt, an official documentation index, or a known relevant official page. Do not use an index entry alone as evidence of transaction behavior.

Use the available retrieval tools to attempt to read a relevant official transaction page. Claim successful verification only after reading evidence that supports it; if retrieval fails, explicitly report the failure.

Support any claimed transaction semantics with a citation to the specific official page actually read and a matching explanation of its evidence. Do not invent a citation or cite llms.txt as behavioral evidence. If verification was blocked, do not fabricate a verified conclusion.

Keep the conclusion within what the retrieved evidence establishes. If retrieval fails or the evidence does not establish the claim, say it remains unverified. No uncertainty disclaimer is required for a claim that was actually verified.
evals.covers: Documentation · Verify claims against a relevant page, not the index
